quote: I've been looking at it for since my husband died five years ago.
stewart_read: This is a trust-gift disclosure per schema — grief plus financial exploitation — and the rep moves straight into design-pitch language without acknowledging it.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be intentionally not dwelling to avoid seeming exploitative himself, but the transcript shows no acknowledgment at all, not even a brief one.
coaching_implication: Suggested rephrase (not verbatim): pause, acknowledge the loss specifically, then bridge — 'I'm sorry to hear that. That makes sense why you'd be careful about who you trust with this.'

quote: everybody jumped on the bandwagon, won all of my money.
stewart_read: This names the actual root objection — being scammed while grieving — and the rep's next line (02:58) is a generic 'I totally understand where you're coming from' rather than a direct name-and-bridge.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply didn't have a scam-encounter rebuttal ready. No evidence rep was deliberately deferring this.
coaching_implication: This maps to protocols.scam_encounter_reference (TBD in schema) — Ion needs an exemplar phrasing for 'I've been scammed before' disclosures; rep needed to name it specifically, not generically.

quote: I'm 80 years old, and I don't know how much time I've got left on this earth.
stewart_read: A second distinct vulnerability disclosure (age/mortality/estate) stacked on top of the grief disclosure, again met with no direct acknowledgment before the rep pivots to a qualifier question.
coaching_implication: Each new vulnerability disclosure that goes unacknowledged adds a brick to the wall the customer is building toward disengagement — cumulative effect, not isolated miss.

quote: Right now, I can't afford no solar.
stewart_read: Textbook trigger for the 'can't afford it' flip (what you can't afford is your current bill), but rep instead explains the payment-swap mechanism — a feature explanation, not an inversion.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep's response at 00:20 is a soft version of the inversion strategy (bill-swap framing) even if not the sharp flip language — partial credit, not a clean miss.
coaching_implication: Coach the sharper flip: 'What you can't afford is what you're already paying the utility every month' lands harder than explaining the mechanics first.

quote: I've looked at everybody's designs and everything.
stewart_read: Customer discloses she's seen multiple companies' designs online already — a competitive-context signal the rep never probes (which companies, what they showed, why she didn't move forward).
alternative_hypothesis: Given the call was already ending, probing here may have been low-yield — but the schema still marks unprobed prior-design disclosures as a miss.
coaching_implication: Even in a losing call, a quick 'what did those look like, did any of them show real savings numbers?' could have surfaced why she never converted before.

quote: right now, inside of my house, it looks like a hoarder's home
stewart_read: A third vulnerability disclosure (home condition tied to grief/downsizing) again met with a flat 'Gotcha' before the rep concedes and removes her from the list.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive: by this point rep may have correctly read the call as unsalvageable and chosen a clean, respectful exit — the concession itself may be the right call given three stacked barriers.
coaching_implication: The exit itself (04:56) was graceful and non-pushy, which is good; but nothing in the call acknowledged her disclosures by name before disengaging.

quote: No. You're totally good. I understand. I'll I'll take you off for now.
stewart_read: The call ends with no locked next step, no text-follow-up promise, and no attempt to leave a door open beyond a generic 'reach back out.'
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer's repeated and escalating objections, a hard close attempt may have been more damaging than a soft graceful exit — this may be the appropriate move given her stated barriers.
coaching_implication: Even on a clean DQ-by-circumstance, schema calls for a specific next-step anchor (e.g., 'I'll check back with you in a few months') rather than an open-ended 'reach back out.'
